results.title: Beijing has supported Moscow but 'China understands that America is way more important than Russia'
results.content: Following Xi Jinping's very friendly rare tarmac greeting for Donald Trump, Erin Ogunkeye is pleased to welcome Kerry Brown, Professor of Chinese Studies and Director of the Lau China Institute at King's College, London. Brown examines the complex relationship between the world's two largest economies, China's growing diplomatic influence and the competition over artificial intelligence.“China is the diplomatic center of the world,” says Brown, pointing to Beijing's ability to bring together leaders from Russia, the United States, Europe and elsewhere. He argues that China now has “extraordinary convening power" and significant influence over Russia.

results.title: French ex-PM Philippe pledges to slash spending, hike retirement age as Elysée bid falters
results.content: Former prime minister Édouard Philippe pledged on Wednesday to slash public spending, scrap France’s statutory 35-hour workweek and raise the retirement age to 65 from the current 62.9 years as he unveiled a slew of measures aimed a staving off economic "catastrophe" for France. An early frontrunner in next year's presidential election, Philippe is now trailing rivals in opinion polls and at risk of missing out on the second-round runoff.

results.title: War in Ukraine: Is France in direct conflict with Russia?
results.content: An investigation published by the French public radio channel RFI on November 17 revealed that a confidential mission by the French army known as "Volia" has been used for months to conceal the presence of French personnel in Ukraine. Russia was prompt to accuse France of direct involvement in the conflict. Is this true?

results.title: Senate leadership challenge exposes divisions among Democrat
results.content: As Democrats prepare to take control of the Senate, incumbent minority leader Chuck Schumer is facing an insurgent leadership bid from Senator Chris Van Hollen and disputes over party leadership are exposing divisions over what direction to take the Democratic party after their midterms sweep.

results.title: Russia’s new low-cost munitions pose a fresh threat to Ukraine
results.content: Dan-T, Filin and Geran-5 might not mean anything to you, but in Ukraine, everyone is talking about these munitions. These new Russian weapons are small, fast and cheap – and a major threat, as they were specially designed to get around Ukrainian anti-aircraft defences and strike deep within the country.

results.title: Israel begins new military operation in Gaza
results.content: Israeli tanks advanced in an area of the central Gaza Strip on Wednesday, witnesses said, and the Israeli military said its ​forces were targeting ‌Hamas infrastructure outside the "Yellow Line" that sets the boundary of the part of the enclave controlled by Israel "The IDF launched a precise operation within the Gaza Strip earlier today west of the Yellow Line... to remove a threat posed to IDF troops operating in the Gaza Strip," the military said.

results.title: Gazans flee shelters as Israeli army launches ground operation beyond Yellow Line
results.content: Palestinians fled their tents and shelters in central Gaza on Wednesday after Israel launched a rare ground operation in an area it withdrew ​from under a ‌2025 ceasefire. The Israeli army said it crossed the Yellow Line separating Israeli and Hamas-controlled areas "to remove a threat posed to IDF troops operating in the Gaza Strip".

results.title: Yemen: Why the Houthis may besiege Aden rather than storm it
results.content: Bolstered by their recent military successes, Houthi rebels this week advanced close to the southern port city of Aden, the interim capital of the internationally recognised Yemeni government. Amid territorial ambitions, regional rivalries, and divisions within government forces, the potential fall of this stronghold could permanently alter the balance of power in the country.

results.title: 🔴 US Democrats nominate Hakeem Jeffries to be first Black speaker of the House
US Democrats nominate Hakeem Jeffries to be first Black speaker of the House
results.content: Democrats nominated Hakeem Jeffries on Wednesday to be the next speaker of the House of Representatives, putting him on track to make history as the nation’s first Black American with the gavel.

results.title: French presidential elections 2027: More candidates, more confusion (Episode 2)
results.content: France will head to the polls to vote for its next president in the spring of 2027. Thirty-eight candidates are currently vying to make it onto the final ballot and have until March 12 to gather backing from 500 elected officials. One figure currently stands out: Marine Le Pen. The far-right National Rally leader has a significant lead in the latest polls.

results.title: WHO sounds alarm over antibiotic resistance
results.content: The World Health Organization sounded the alarm Monday over antimicrobial resistance, saying the world is off pace to meet key 2030 targets. Many countries have long neglected funding to track and detect dangerous microbes that resist antibiotic treatment, according to a report by the body.

results.title: Xi embraces Trump in China: 'Diplomacy playing out in real time'
results.content: President Xi Jinping personally greeted US counterpart Donald Trump on the tarmac at a Chinese airport on Wednesday, with the two leaders briefly hugging ahead of their highly anticipated meeting with Russia's Vladimir Putin. Reporting from Shenzhen, France 24's Jan Camenzind Broomby says the warm greeting was a "big sign of respect" from Xi but also a calculated component of diplomatic efforts.

results.title: Xi welcomes Trump to China ahead of high-stakes Putin meeting
results.content: President Xi Jinping personally greeted US counterpart Donald Trump on the tarmac at a Chinese airport on Wednesday, with the two leaders briefly hugging ahead of their highly anticipated meeting with Russia's Vladimir Putin. Beijing has indicated the war in Ukraine will not be discussed during the trilateral meeting, but Trump had said the conflict would find its way onto the agenda, something that experts say is likely to please Putin.

results.title: Three leaders, three agendas: Who wants what from Xi-Trump-Putin summit?
results.content: Be it curbing arms sales to Taiwan, bouncing back after a midterms shellacking, or the optics of a place at the table with the world's two superpowers, Xi Jinping, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin are approaching their trilateral meeting in Shenzhen with starkly different aims and agendas. Here's a look at what the Chinese, US and Russian leaders are hoping for.

results.title: US strikes Iranian island after Tehran targets Bahrain
results.content: The US and Iran exchanged fire on Tuesday, with the US striking an Iranian missile launch site after Iran said it targeted a US military radar system in Bahrain, despite talks between Iran and mediators Oman and Qatar.

results.title: Why are measles cases soaring in the US?
results.content: The United States has lost its long-held status of having eradicated measles as cases of the dangerous and highly contagious virus soar around the country. It follows accusations by medical experts that US President Donald Trump and his health secretary, noted vaccine skeptic Robert F. Kennedy Jr, have fanned distrust in vaccinations, leading to an decline on the number of children getting inoculated against the disease.

results.title: Robert Pattinson is the new James Bond: The surprise casting choice explained
results.content: Robert Pattinson will be the new James Bond, taking over from Daniel Craig in one of cinema’s most iconic roles. Film critic Emma Jones joins Eve Jackson on the arts24 weekly film show to discuss the surprise choice, Pattinson's star power and what he could bring to 007. Plus, they review the latest "Hunger Games" prequel "Sunrise on the Reaping", Lukas Dhont's Cannes prize winner "Coward" and Germany's Oscar entry "Everytime".

results.title: The calisson: A sweet taste of France's Provence region
results.content: If you've ever visited the south of France, you may have come across a calisson. These traditional yellow and white almond-shaped candies are everywhere in the region. We tell you all about them with our guest Alexis Bertucat, head of communication and tourism for renowned calisson maker Confiserie du Roy René.

results.title: Democrat Mary Peltola wins Alaska Senate race in historic victory
results.content: Democrat Mary Peltola won Alaska's US Senate race on Tuesday, projections from US media showed, defeating Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan and becoming the first Democrat to win a US ‌Senate seat in the state in nearly 20 years and the first Alaska Native ever to do so.

results.title: 'A not so veiled criticism of the US' as Xi blasts protectionism at APEC summit
results.content: China's President Xi Jinping on Wednesday pledged to stand up against trade protectionism and said regional economies needed to stand up to rising unilateralism in what France 24's Kethevane Gorjestani says was a "a not so veiled criticism of the US". Xi's comments came APEC summit in Shenzhen, China, where a highly anticipated trilateral meeting between Xi, Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin is set to take place on Thursday.

results.title: North Korea completes external works on enrichment facility extension, says IAEA
results.content: A new extension to North Korea's Yongbyon enrichment facility has been "externally complete" since mid-October, according to the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA), which relies on satellite imagery and open sources to monitor the country's nuclear programme. IAEA chief Rafael Grossi on Wednesday said expansion of Pyongyang's enrichment programme remains "cause for serious concern".

results.title: 'Extreme wealth can become a type of brain damage': Journalist Alexander Hurst
results.content: An international journalist who poured his meagre savings into highly risky options trading at the start of the Covid-19 pandemic and quickly made $1.2 million, before losing it all again, has spoken to FRANCE 24 about his experience. Alexander Hurst works for a number of media outlets, including the Guardian as a correspondent based in Paris.

results.title: Athlete support under spotlight as South Africa swimmer switches to Netherlands
results.content: South Africa's sports minister said Tuesday he had ordered an investigation into the national swimming federation following the departure of the country's most decorated Olympic athlete, swimmer Tatjana Smith, for the Netherlands. In an emotional video on social media, the 29-year-old two-time Olympic gold medallist announced last week she would no longer represent South Africa at international events because of financial challenges.
